note: Concrete replay briefs. Source identifiers and URLs were verified on 2026-09-06; a run must retrieve and preserve the current source text rather than treating this manifest as evidence.

inputs.question: In adults with chronic kidney disease, what do the active EMPA-KIDNEY trial and its post-trial follow-up establish about the durability of empagliflozin's kidney and cardiovascular effects?

inclusionCriteria: Reports of EMPA-KIDNEY (NCT03594110) with clinical or kidney-function outcomes
Current CKD guidance used only for practice context
exclusionCriteria: Commentaries without new EMPA-KIDNEY outcome data

mustDo: Declare the review design, actual searches, eligibility and protocol status.
Keep three publications as separate reports but count NCT03594110 as one primary study.
Keep the guideline outside the primary-study count and distinguish randomized from post-trial observation.
Restate each quoted estimate with the quote's own numbers, and answer every review finding marked 需回应 in the submission's responses.
mustNotDo: Add the same randomized participants three times.
Describe post-trial treatment exposure as randomized after the active trial ended.
State a comparison its own numbers contradict: the 2026-09-08 run wrote that the post-trial hazard ratio of 0.87 was smaller than the in-trial 0.72.

inputs.question: For adults receiving oral aripiprazole, is there direct prospective evidence that routine structured screening for impulse-control symptoms prevents patient harm?

sources.role: US label warning and management context

replaySearches.query: aripiprazole structured impulse-control screening prevention prospective trial

replaySearches.reason: Fixture simulates a registry gateway timeout; the run must retain the actual response when executed.

mustDo: Keep the successful zero-hit query separate from unavailable registry access.
State that label warnings and case reports do not establish the effectiveness of a screening programme.
Name the prospective comparative evidence that would answer the prevention question.
mustNotDo: Interpret the registry timeout as proof that no trials exist.
Convert post-marketing reports into an incidence estimate or a proven preventive effect.

inputs.question: What prognostic models for mortality in adult sepsis have been evaluated with MIMIC-IV, and can their reported MIMIC-IV validation cohorts be treated as independent evidence?

sources.role: HALP mortality model with MIMIC-IV validation
intra-abdominal sepsis mortality model using MIMIC-IV and eICU

mustDo: Preserve each publication and its stated database role while leaving patient-cohort overlap unresolved when dates and cohort definitions cannot be verified.
Record the two model publications as abstract-level evidence until full text is preserved.
Explain which cohort dates, identifiers and eligibility definitions are needed to establish independence.
mustNotDo: Call the two model abstracts full text.
Treat use of the same public database as either proof of identical cohorts or proof of independent cohorts.

inputs.question: Write a narrative review, in English and in exactly this outline, of what the EMPA-KIDNEY trial reports reviewed here establish about empagliflozin in adults with chronic kidney disease: Background; Certainty of the evidence; Benefits and harms; Values and preferences; Resource use; Equity and feasibility; Conclusions and practice points.

mustDo: Keep the requested outline as the report's level-two sections, in its order and under its own English names, then add only the apparatus the outline leaves out (Abstract, Methods, Limitations, References).
Write the Values and preferences section as a section of the review, with its claims cited like any other; the numbered reference list is the last section and is the only one headed References.
Give the practice points their own section after the conclusions, with a cited claim on every action line and no derived estimate in it.
State a certainty level for each outcome only where a named instrument was applied, and say which.
mustNotDo: Rename, merge, reorder or drop a requested section so that a checker reads the report more easily.
Write a Chinese heading, label or sentence anywhere in the report (or a Chinese gloss of a name that the English text does not need).
Condition the instruction to call emergency services on whether a medicine worked.
